title: locality-sensitive-admission-prefetch-reserve-operator-drain-bridge
author: Diego Alvarez
release_notes: Adds locality-sensitive admission controller with a two-stage (fastpath + reserve) admission flow, a proactive prefetch reserve for hot key KV caches, an operator-facing drain bridge to toggle emergency soft-evacuations, and telemetry/SLI adjustments. Backwards-compatible config defaults; opt-in via cluster flags.
description:
Motivation: During a recent regional instability incident we observed thrashing between failover and regional rejoin which amplified tail latency for medium-sized tenants. This PR implements a locality-sensitive admission controller that (1) prefers fastpath admission for locally warm sessions, (2) keeps a small proactive prefetch reserve for hot KV prefixes to reduce first-token latency on rejoin, and (3) adds an operator drain bridge to trigger a controlled soft-evacuation window without hard dropping connections. The design aims to reduce SLO breaches during partial regional degradations by avoiding wide blast-radius admission changes and by giving operators a safe manual control for emergency soft drains.

What this changes (single-line summary): locality_admitter runtime + prefetch reserve + operator drain bridge + telemetry and rollout hooks.

Detailed notes:
- New two-stage admission pipeline in runtime/admission: fastpath decision (local cache warm & probe pass) falls back to reserve admission slot when local resources are exhausted.
- Proactive prefetch reserve: a tiny reservoir (configurable, default 25 slots per AZ) that will prefetch KV prefixes for tenants with high recent affinity to smooth first-request latencies after rejoin.
- Operator drain bridge: ops can flip a boolean on the control plane to initiate a soft-evacuation mode; the bridge coordinates with admission to drain new fastpath admits into reserve mode over a controlled grace window.
- Telemetry: new SLIs and tags added: admission.path (fastpath|reserve|rejected), prefetch.hit, prefetch.fill_latency_ms, operator.drain_active. Dashboards and alerts updated accordingly.
- Backwards compatibility: default flags keep previous behavior unless the cluster flag enable_locality_admit=true is set. Operator bridge is gated by RBAC and requires an ops-signed policy in the control plane.
- Rollout plan: staged rollout via canary in staging, then 25% production AZs, then global. Includes a kill-switch path that disables prefetch if prefetch miss rate exceeds threshold to avoid extra egress costs.

Checklist:
- [x] Core admission algorithm implemented
- [x] Operator bridge + RBAC gating
- [x] Telemetry emitted and dashboards updated
- [x] Unit and integration tests covering edge cases
- [x] Documented operator runbook and rollback steps (docs/ops)
- [x] Feature gated behind cluster flag

Incident tie-in: SUP-1223 documented that tenants experienced elevated p95 after a partial-region control-plane disconnect. This change was developed to reduce the number of tenants escalated during that pattern.

Testing and CI: Unit tests exercised specific fastpath/reserve transitions. Integration harness includes simulated region partition where we assert stall-free rejoin for 90% of seeded tenants. CI initially reported a flaky integration test (TestAdmissionRace) related to timing; I fixed it by using a deterministic clock stub and re-ran the pipeline which passed.

Migration/ops instructions (short): enable flag enable_locality_admit=false by default. To opt-in in a cluster: flip flag -> deploy runtime with operator_bridge enabled -> observe admission.path rates in the canary -> enable prefetch reserve on success. To emergency-disable prefetch: control-plane API /ops/feature/disable_prefetch with confirmation header. See docs/ops/runbooks/locality-admit.md for full steps.

Related work: builds on the admission abstractions introduced in ENG-3780 and the prefetched-kv prototype from ENG-4312. See linked Linear items for context.

review_comments: Asha Mehta: Overall design looks good. Question: what guarantees do we give to reserved-slot tenants when the prefetch reservoir is exhausted? We need a clear SLA for reserve rejects so higher layers can decide to fallback or degrade gracefully.

Diego Alvarez (author): Reply: reserve admission is best-effort; when exhausted we return a soft-degrade signal (AdmissionResult::ThrottleWithHint) with a suggested retry-after and an opt-in hint to fall back to read-only mode. I've added explicit contract docs in runtime/admission/README and a test in tenant_reservoir_test.go.
Liam O'Connor: Telemetry naming looks consistent but prefer admission.path tag to be instrumented as a histogram for latency breakdown rather than plain counter. Can we emit both?
Diego Alvarez (author): Updated: admission.path is now both a counter and a tagged histogram. Added admission.path_latency_ms histogram in telemetry/metrics_registry.yaml.
Mariana Santos: Operator bridge needs RBAC checks in the control-plane handler. Ensure the ops CLI respects the same RBAC and logs actions for audit.
Diego Alvarez (author): Added RBAC gating and audit entries; operator CLI now requires --confirm and logs the initiating principal. See docs/ops/runbooks/locality-admit.md for examples.
merge_details: Merged via squash on 2026-02-23 by Asha Mehta. Squash commit: 5e2c9b8. Merge strategy: squash. Post-merge actions: staged rollout started (canary in us-west-2), dashboard created and alert thresholds lowered for initial observation window. No rollback needed during canary.
notes_for_reviewer: Key areas to double-check: deterministic clock usage in tests (avoid flakiness), RBAC audit entries for operator bridge, prefetch reservoir sizing defaults and cost model. If you want a narrower default reservoir, change default in runtime/prefetch/config.go before cutting the production rollout.
